sources.role: GTK/Unix, Win32 and macOS config, controller, save/state and BIOS contracts
official CI/platform matrix (Windows, Linux GTK/X11, macOS)
Flatpak app id com.snes9x.Snes9x, GTK command, home access and pinned source build

paths.path: ~/.config/snes9x/snes9x.conf (GTK frontend; $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/snes9x/snes9x.conf when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is set). The legacy X11 frontend instead uses ~/.snes9x/snes9x.conf
paths.naming: ConfigFile text sections Display, Sound, Files, Window State, Netplay, Behavior, Emulation, Controls, and Joypad 0..9; Files::SRAMDirectory and Files::SaveStateDirectory are empty by default, meaning ROM-relative storage

paths.path: ~/.config/snes9x/snes9x.conf (or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/snes9x/snes9x.conf); legacy X11 uses ~/.snes9x/snes9x.conf
paths.naming: GTK: [Joypad 0]..[Joypad 9] keys Up, Down, Left, Right, Start, Select, A, B, X, Y, L, R, Turbo A/B/X/Y/L/R, Sticky A/B/X/Y/L/R; [Shortcuts] uses emulator names. Values are `Keyboard <GDK key name>` optionally `Shift+/Ctrl+/Alt+`, `Joystick <1-based device> Button <n>`, or `Joystick <1-based device> Axis <axis> +/- <percent>` (e.g. Keyboard x or Joystick 1 Button 0)
evidence: source:gtk/src/gtk_config.cpp writes each Joypad N binding and Shortcuts section @7a8878f1
source:unix/unix.cpp keymaps legacy X11 J00:B... grammar @7a8878f1

paths.path: ROM directory by default (GTK Files::SRAMDirectory empty); otherwise the directory selected in Files::SRAMDirectory
paths.naming: <ROM stem>.srm battery SRAM and <ROM stem>.rtc real-time-clock data; BS-X fallback is BS-X.srm. SRAM directory and filename are generated by S9xGetFilename
evidence: source:gtk/src/gtk_file.cpp S9xGetDirectory(SRAM_DIR) falls back to ROM filename directory and S9xGetFilename(.srm) @7a8878f1

paths.path: ROM directory by default (GTK Files::SaveStateDirectory empty); otherwise the directory selected in Files::SaveStateDirectory
paths.naming: Quick slots are <ROM stem>.000 through <ROM stem>.010 (11 slots); explicit freezes use <ROM stem>.<three-digit>.frz, and undo uses <ROM stem>.undo. GTK save-state dialog also accepts a user-selected .sst/.frz path
evidence: source:gtk/src/gtk_file.cpp SNAPSHOT_DIR falls back to ROM directory @7a8878f1
source:controls.cpp QuickLoad000..QuickLoad010 and S9xGetFilename three-digit extension @7a8878f1

paths.path: No BIOS required for ordinary SNES cartridges. Optional files are looked up in the configured BIOS_DIR; GTK defaults an unset BIOS directory to the ROM directory, while the legacy Unix frontend creates ~/.snes9x/bios
paths.naming: Optional Satellaview BIOS: BS-X.bin or BS-X.bios; optional ST-0010/ST-V-style data: STBIOS.bin. No authoritative canonical checksum is supplied by this source tree; normal SNES play has no external firmware requirement
evidence: source:memmap.cpp STBIOS.bin lookup and bsx.cpp BS-X.bin/BS-X.bios lookup @7a8878f1
source:gtk/src/gtk_file.cpp unset BIOS_DIR falls back to ROM directory @7a8878f1

paths.path: not applicable
paths.naming: Snes9x does not consume an external cryptographic key file.

linux.notes: The official Linux build matrix includes GTK and X11 frontends; this record describes both config roots where they differ. The GTK frontend is the one packaged by Flathub.

paths.path: ~/.var/app/com.snes9x.Snes9x/config/snes9x/snes9x.conf (Flatpak XDG_CONFIG_HOME plus the GTK `snes9x` directory)
paths.naming: Same ConfigFile sections as native GTK, including Files::SRAMDirectory and Files::SaveStateDirectory; values are persisted in the text snes9x.conf

paths.path: ~/.var/app/com.snes9x.Snes9x/config/snes9x/snes9x.conf
paths.naming: GTK [Joypad 0]..[Joypad 9] and [Shortcuts] mappings; values use `Keyboard <GDK key>`, `Joystick <1-based device> Button <n>`, or `Joystick <1-based device> Axis <axis> +/- <percent>`

paths.path: Beside the loaded ROM in the host-visible game directory by default; `--filesystem=home` allows normal home-library ROM paths. Files::SRAMDirectory can override
paths.naming: <ROM stem>.srm plus optional <ROM stem>.rtc; BS-X fallback BS-X.srm
evidence: source:gtk/src/gtk_file.cpp default SRAM_DIR is ROM directory and .srm naming @7a8878f1

paths.path: Beside the loaded ROM by default; Files::SaveStateDirectory can override
paths.naming: <ROM stem>.000..010 quick slots and <ROM stem>.<three-digit>.frz freeze files; .undo is the GTK undo state
evidence: source:gtk/src/gtk_file.cpp default SNAPSHOT_DIR is ROM directory @7a8878f1
source:controls.cpp quick save/load uses three-digit slots @7a8878f1

paths.path: No external BIOS required for ordinary SNES cartridges; optional BIOS_DIR files are user supplied and, with an unset GTK BIOS directory, resolve beside the ROM
paths.naming: Optional BS-X.bin or BS-X.bios and STBIOS.bin; no authoritative canonical checksum exists in the upstream source
evidence: source:memmap.cpp and bsx.cpp optional BIOS filenames @7a8878f1

paths.path: not applicable
paths.naming: Snes9x does not consume an external cryptographic key file.

linux-flatpak.notes: Flathub's community package uses the GTK frontend and grants home access. Flatpak changes the XDG config root, but ROM-relative saves/states remain next to the ROM unless the user configures another directory.

paths.path: ~/Library/Preferences/com.snes9x.macos.snes9x.plist (NSUserDefaults standard domain; bundle identifier from the macOS Xcode target)
paths.naming: NSUserDefaults dictionaries KeyboardConfig (numeric Snes9x button code -> macOS virtual key code), JoypadInputs, and JoypadPlayers plus display/emulation preference keys

paths.path: ~/Library/Preferences/com.snes9x.macos.snes9x.plist
paths.naming: KeyboardConfig maps numeric `button + kNumButtons * player` keys to macOS virtual key codes; JoypadPlayers maps player number to `vendorID:productID:index`; JoypadInputs maps that device key to `buttonCode -> cookie:value` controller events

paths.path: ~/Library/Application Support/Snes9x/SRAMs/<ROM stem>.srm by default (saveInROMFolder=2); the user can select ROM folder or a custom folder
paths.naming: <ROM stem>.srm battery SRAM and <ROM stem>.rtc; application-support folder name is SRAMs (legacy uppercase SNES9X folder is honored). No canonical checksum applies to saves

paths.path: ~/Library/Application Support/Snes9x/Freezes/<ROM stem>.<three-digit>.frz by default (saveInROMFolder=2); ROM/custom folder choices are supported
paths.naming: <ROM stem>.000.frz through .999.frz (S9xGetFreezeFilename formats three digits); application-support folder name is Freezes

paths.path: No BIOS required for ordinary SNES cartridges. Optional BIOSes folder is ~/Library/Application Support/Snes9x/BIOSes by default; the source calls it a dummy directory selector
paths.naming: Optional BS-X.bin or BS-X.bios and STBIOS.bin where relevant; no authoritative canonical checksum is published in this source
evidence: source:macosx/mac-file.mm .bio selector maps to BIOSes and FindApplicationSupportFolder @7a8878f1

paths.path: not applicable
paths.naming: Snes9x does not consume an external cryptographic key file.

paths.path: <directory containing snes9x.exe>\snes9x.conf (the current Win32 port writes the text config beside the executable; relative directory defaults are resolved from that directory)
paths.naming: ConfigFile sections include Settings\Win, Settings\Win\Files, Controls\Win, Controls\Win\Hotkeys; the file is plain text and is atomically backed up during save
evidence: source:win32/wconfig.cpp S9xSaveConfigFile uses S9xGetDirectory(DEFAULT_DIR) + snes9x.conf and WinRegisterConfigItems sections @7a8878f1

paths.path: <directory containing snes9x.exe>\snes9x.conf
paths.naming: Controls\Win keys are Joypad1:Up/Down/Left/Right/A/B/Y/X/L/R/Start/Select plus diagonal and turbo entries; values are keyboard names/virtual-key strings (e.g. A, SPACE) or joystick tokens `(J<hex-device>)Button <n>` / `(J<hex-device>)X axis +/-`, serialized by TranslateKey. Controls\Win\Hotkeys stores Key:<action> and Mods:<action>
evidence: source:win32/wconfig.cpp ADD2/ADDT macros define JoypadN:<control> and hotkey names; CIT_VKEY serialization @7a8878f1
source:win32/InputCustom.cpp TranslateKey emits `(J%x)`, Button and axis grammar @7a8878f1

paths.path: <directory containing snes9x.exe>\Saves by default (Settings\Win\Files Dir:SRAM = .\Saves); user can configure an absolute or relative directory
paths.naming: <ROM stem>.srm battery SRAM, plus <ROM stem>.rtc where applicable; legacy load fallback checks ROM directory if configured SRAM file is absent
evidence: source:win32/wsnes9x.cpp SaveSRAM/LoadSRAM uses S9xGetFilename(.srm, SRAM_DIR) with ROM fallback @7a8878f1

paths.path: <directory containing snes9x.exe>\Saves by default (Settings\Win\Files Dir:Savestates = .\Saves); user configurable
paths.naming: <ROM stem>.000.frz through <ROM stem>.999.frz for three-digit freeze slots; current slot and save/load hotkeys are persisted in Controls\Win\Hotkeys
evidence: source:win32/wconfig.cpp Dir:Savestates default .\Saves and SaveSlot0..SaveSlot9 registrations @7a8878f1

paths.path: <directory containing snes9x.exe>\BIOS by default (Settings\Win\Files Dir:Bios = .\BIOS); user configurable
paths.naming: Optional BS-X.bios or BS-X.bin and STBIOS.bin; no authoritative canonical checksum is published in the upstream source. Ordinary SNES cartridge emulation needs no external firmware
evidence: source:bsx.cpp and memmap.cpp optional BIOS names @7a8878f1

paths.path: not applicable
paths.naming: Snes9x does not consume an external cryptographic key file.

notes: This record distinguishes the actively packaged GTK/Win32/macOS frontends. Snes9x has no mandatory SNES BIOS; BS-X and STBIOS are optional special-hardware files and the upstream tree does not publish one canonical checksum for them. The GTK Flatpak is community packaging, not an upstream release, and its sandbox home permission is captured from the pinned manifest.
